exposure: Mode of delivery (cesarean delivery vs. spontaneous vaginal delivery)
outcome: Psychometric properties of the Japanese version of the Obstetric Quality of Recovery-10 scoring tool
finding: Inpatient postpartum recovery is significantly better in the first 2 postpartum days following spontaneous vaginal delivery compared with scheduled cesarean delivery, with recovery largely achieved within 4 days for cesarean and 3 days for vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Women who had a spontaneous vaginal delivery had better quality of recovery in the first two days postpartum, prolonged time to analgesia requirement, decreased opioid consumption, reduced antiemetic requirement, and reduced times to liquid/solid intake, ambulation, and discharge compared to those who delivered via cesarean.
gest_age: Measured, but specific values not provided
